commit.message:
fix(web): allow only one new document create at a time (#3742)

A click repeated, or the New dialog reopened, while a create was in
flight started another create. "New cover letter instead" had no
pending state at all, so it stayed enabled and each extra click added a
letter.

useStartDocument now runs Start blank, Try a sample and New cover
letter through one guard shared by every caller, and the letter button
is disabled while a create runs.

feat: add entry header layouts, row order and accents (#3689)

* feat: add entry header layouts, row order and accents

Add an Entries group to the Design panel on the web, the phone design
sheet and the mobile app. Experience, Education and Volunteer headers can
use Stacked (now the default on every template, Meowth included), One
line, Compact, Date column or Eyebrow. Row order puts the role before the
organization for Experience and Education, from the panel or the preview's
Editing tag. Accent adds a rule, bar or band in the accent color. Date
column also moves the dates of Projects, Awards, Certifications and
Publications.

The settings live in the optional metadata.design.entry, read through
entryHeaderOf so older resumes keep the stacked layout. The Semantic CSS
tree follows the effective layout, so existing selectors keep working; the
one-line parts move from Meowth to every template. One line and Date column
fall back to Stacked in the sidebar and in multi-column sections. Title rows
align on the text baseline, One line wraps instead of squeezing, and wrapped
dates and locations stay at the row's end.

DOCX and ODT exports follow the row order. Meowth previews, guides, the
OpenAPI spec and the schema references are regenerated.

commit.message:
perf(web): paint prerendered pages before loading the app

Prerendered pages requested the entry script and about 44 module preloads from the head, and
Lighthouse's simulation counted them toward the largest paint, so mobile scores swung between 0.6
and 0.99. They now start the app from a small inline loader after the first contentful paint (with a
3 s fallback), adding the preloads at that moment so the entry's imports still download in parallel.

Also:
- The ATS checker's first state no longer fades in on load; the fade held its largest paint until
  the app had loaded.
- The template gallery's first row loads eagerly and its first preview at high priority.
- Doodles get quarter-size files and declare the width each is drawn at, and the doodles on the
  first screen load at high priority.

Local Lighthouse, same machine: homepage mobile 0.75 to 0.88 and desktop 0.95 to 1.0, ATS checker
mobile 0.74 to 0.98, templates mobile 0.76 to 0.96.

fix(web): stop zod's eval probe from reporting a CSP violation

before any module loads; it couldn't compile under this policy anyway. The server allows the script

commit.message:
perf(server): serve brotli, send Early Hints links and purge Cloudflare by tag

- The Docker build writes brotli copies of the web app's text files and WASM
  (tooling/docker/precompress.mjs), and the static handler serves them with `precompressed: true`.
  Browsers that accept brotli get the startup JS about 13% smaller and the PDF engine's WASM 26%
  smaller; others still get gzip on the fly.
- Page responses carry preload `Link` headers for the page's stylesheet and fonts, which Cloudflare
  sends ahead of the page as 103 Early Hints.
- Pages are tagged `Cache-Tag: html` and fixed-name public files `Cache-Tag: public`. A release now
  purges those two tags instead of the whole zone, so hashed /assets files stay cached across
  releases. Purge everything once after the first release with tags, since earlier cache entries
  carry none.
- The Content Security Policy allows Cloudflare Web Analytics' beacon from
  static.cloudflareinsights.com, for real-user Core Web Vitals.
- Removes the unused /videos immutable-cache rule.

commit.message:
ci(turbo): share build results through Vercel Remote Cache

Main-branch CI and Docker image builds now read and write Turbo's remote cache
with short-lived OIDC tokens; pull requests keep the Actions cache only. The
token reaches the image build as a BuildKit secret, since provenance records
build args, and the build no longer forces a rebuild.

Docker builds compute the same task hashes as a checkout: the builder stage
restores the root package.json that prune rewrites, .gitignore, and the global
dependency files. The build task also hashes the root package.json, whose
version web and server embed; before, a version-only release commit could
restore the previous build.
